Make docugate init the one command a developer runs to set up everything, with as little friction as possible. Keep tour init, tour serve and tour export working on their own. Node built-ins only; follow the style of src/init.ts and src/tour-init.ts.

1. src/tour-install.ts and docugate tour install: add the DocuGate pill loader to the app, marked with <!-- docugate:pill --> comments so it can be found again.
   - An index.html at the repo root or in frontend/, client/, web/, app/ or public/ (skip node_modules, dist, build, .next): insert before </body> a small inline script that loads http://localhost:<port>/pill.js only when location.hostname is localhost or 127.0.0.1, so it never loads in production.
   - Next.js (app/layout.tsx|jsx or src/app/layout.tsx|jsx, else pages/_document.tsx|jsx): add a <script> loading the same URL, rendered only when process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'.
   - Nothing found: print the one line to paste.
   Running it twice changes nothing; --remove takes it out; --port defaults to 4178. It never touches any other part of the file.
2. docugate init runs the whole setup in order, one short question at a time in a terminal:
   a. Asks "Is this repository the frontend, the backend, or both?" (or --role) and saves "role" in docugate.json with the docs folder, as today. docugate.json is meant to be committed, so a second run skips questions already answered.
   b. Leaves a clearly marked place for "sign in to DocuGate and connect this repository" (built in a later task); for now print that this step is coming.
   c. If the role is frontend or both: offers to write the tour with IBM Bob (the existing tourInit), then runs tour install. If the role is backend: skips both and says the frontend repository's tour can point into this one.
   d. Ends with a short summary of what changed and the next command: docugate tour serve.
   --yes accepts every default without asking. With no terminal (CI), it asks nothing and only writes docugate.json.3. docugate tour serve prints a hint to run docugate tour install when no pill snippet is found.

Tests in test/tour-install.test.mjs and test/init-flow.test.mjs with small fixture projects (Vite, Next app router, Next pages router, nothing found, backend role), covering insert, idempotence, --remove and the init order. Mock Bob the way test/tour-init.test.mjs does. Nothing outside this repository, no scratch scripts or plan files left in the repo root. Done when npm test passes.

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# Mode Switching

You can switch between different modes using the switch_mode tool. Each mode provides access to different capabilities and tools optimized for specific types of tasks.

**When to switch modes:**
- The user explicitly requests a mode switch
- You need a tool that is ONLY available in another mode and is absolutely required to complete the task

**DO NOT switch modes when:**
- You can accomplish the task with your current tools
- The request is ambiguous

Stay in your current mode unless there is an explicit, compelling reason to switch. When in doubt, do not switch.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

For factual questions that require knowledge about IBM products, platforms, languages, commands, APIs, configuration, documented behavior, compatibility, or product-specific errors, consult IBM documentation before answering.
This includes technologies such as IBM i, IBM Z, z/OS, Db2, CICS, COBOL, JCL, RPG, AIX, and watsonx, even when the user does not explicitly say IBM.
For Bob(or IBM Bob) product questions, call `search_ibm_docs` directly with `library_name: "bob"`.
For other IBM products, first call `list_ibm_doc_libraries`, select the most relevant exact library name from its response, and then call `search_ibm_docs`. Do not invent or modify library names.
You may reuse a library name already returned in the current conversation for follow-up questions about the same product.
Base factual product claims on the retrieved documentation. If no suitable library or relevant documentation is found, say so rather than guessing.
Documentation lookup is unnecessary when the request is purely about code in the workspace and does not require IBM product knowledge.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:
{"xAxisData":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[4200,5800,3900]}],"title":"Monthly Revenue"}

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

data.content:
# Create Plan

Follow this structured workflow to produce a high-quality, actionable plan.

## Step 1 — Gather Requirements

Ask the user clarifying questions to fully understand the task:
- What is the goal and expected outcome?
- Are there constraints, preferences, or non-goals?
- Which parts of the codebase are likely involved?
- Any related issues or requirement documents?

Do not proceed until you have enough context to scope the work, be critical of vague intent or requirements.

## Step 2 — Code Search via Sub-Agent

Spawn a `spawn_subagent` of type `"explore"` to research the codebase. The sub-agent should:
- Locate relevant files, symbols, and patterns related to the task
- Identify existing utilities or abstractions that should be reused
- Identify existing design patterns
- Surface any constraints or conventions (e.g. patterns in similar files)

Use the sub-agent's findings to ground your plan in the actual code.

## Step 3 — Clarify Design Intention

Based on the requirements and code research:
- Always confirm your understanding of the intended design with the user
- Raise any open questions or trade-offs that need a decision
- Adjust scope if the code research revealed complexity or simplifications

Do not begin writing the plan document until design intent is confirmed.

## Step 4 — Write the Plan File

Write a structured plan to a markdown file (e.g. `{short-plan-name}-plan.md`). The plan must NOT go into low-level code detail — focus on *what* needs to happen and *why*.

The plan file must include:

### Top-Level Overview
A concise summary of the goal, scope, and approach.

### Sub-Tasks
Break the work into sub-tasks. Each sub-task must have:
- **Intent** — what this sub-task achieves and why
- **Expected Outcomes** — observable results when this sub-task is complete
- **Todo List** — ordered, specific steps to achieve the outcome
- **Relevant Context** — pointers to relevant files, symbols, or patterns
- **Status** — `[ ] pending` (updated to `[x] done` after completion)

Design each sub-task to be processed independently, one at a time, so changes stay focused and reviewable.

## Step 5 — Plan Validation

Before moving to implementation, ensure that the user has fully read the plan. Always ask the user targeted questions to verify the plan is correct and complete:
- Does this plan capture the full scope of the task?
- Are the sub-task boundaries and ordering correct?
- Is any context missing that would be needed during implementation?

Use Mermaid diagrams in chat responses where they clarify architecture or workflow, but do not place Mermaid diagrams directly in the plan file. Avoid double quotes and parentheses inside square brackets in Mermaid syntax.

Refine the plan file based on the user's answers.

## Step 6 — Implementation

Only after the user confirms the plan, recommend implementation by calling the `switch_mode` tool to `agent`.

When explaining how to implement the plan in agent mode:
- Using the `start_subtask` tool, create a new task for each subtask in the <plan-file>.
- In the prompt for the subtask make sure it reads the plan-file to gain the full context around the task.
- After each sub task is complete update the task status in the <plan-file>
- Add any context needed for the next subtask in the <plan-file>
- Wait for the user to check and ok the changes before moving on to the next subtask.

## Reminders

- Ask questions always using the "ask_followup_question" tool
- Never include information without evidence
- Don't include time estimates
Now let me research the codebase to understand the existing patterns before planning.

## DOCUGATE_PACKAGE CODEBASE EXPLORATION SUMMARY

### 1. PROJECT STRUCTURE

**Root Directory Files:**
- `package.json` - Main package manifest (v0.1.3, Node >=18.17)
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript configuration (ES2022, NodeNext modules)
- `README.md`, `LICENSE`
- `.bob/`, `bob_sessions/`, `pill/` - Bob Shell integration & pill UI bundler
- `dist/` - Compiled output (bin: `dist/cli.js`)

**Source Directory (`src/`):**
```
src/
  ├─ cli.ts          # Main CLI entry point (custom arg parser)
  ├─ init.ts         # docugate init command
  ├─ check.ts        # docugate check command
  ├─ config.ts       # docugate.json loader
  ├─ rules.ts        # DocuGate reading rules (mirrors app behavior)
  ├─ openapi.ts      # docugate openapi command
  ├─ tour.ts         # Tour file parser/serializer
  ├─ tour-init.ts    # docugate tour init (Bob Shell integration)
  └─ tour-server.ts  # docugate tour serve (HTTP server)
```

**Test Directory (`test/`):**
```
test/
  ├─ cli.test.mjs              # init, check, openapi commands
  ├─ tour-init.test.mjs        # tour init + Bob Shell mocking
  ├─ tour.test.mjs             # tour parsing/serialization
  ├─ tour-server.test.mjs       # HTTP server handlers
  ├─ pill.test.mjs             # pill UI bundler
  └─ fixtures/
      ├─ tour-parse/           # Sample tour files
      └─ tour-check/           # Full integration test repo
```

---

### 2. CONFIGURATION & SCHEMA

**`docugate.json` Schema** (from `src/rules.ts` & `src/config.ts`):

```typescript
type DocugateConfig = {
  docsDir?: string                   // Docs folder name (default: 'docs')
  title?: string                     // Space title
  sidebar?: string[]                 // List of files/folders for sidebar order
  api?: {
    generate?: {
      from?: string                  // OpenAPI spec path/URL
      output?: string                // Output file (default: 'openapi.json')
      include?: string[]             // Path globs to keep
      exclude?: string[]             // Path globs to drop
      redact?: string[]              // Properties to remove
    }
  }
}

// Known keys set
const KNOWN_KEYS = new Set(['$schema', 'docsDir', 'title', 'sidebar', 'api'])
```

**Config Loading** (`src/config.ts`):
- Reads from `docugate.json` at repository root
- Returns `{ found, config, docsDir, errors, warnings }`
- Validates JSON structure; silently falls back to `docs/` on error
- CLI treats unreadable file as error; server treats as warning

---

### 3. CLI COMMAND REGISTRATION PATTERN

**Custom Parser** (no external CLI library like commander or yargs):

```typescript
// src/cli.ts - Custom argument parsing
type Args = { 
  command?: string
  sub?: string           // For 'tour init', 'tour serve', etc
  sub2?: string          // For 'tour export <file>'
  flags: Map<string, string[]>
  bools: Set<string>
}

const VALUE_FLAGS = new Set([
  'dir', 'title', 'from', 'out', 'include', 'exclude', 'redact', 
  'max-cost', 'team-id', 'port'
])

function parse(argv: string[]): Args { /* custom parsing */ }
```

**Commands Registered:**
```
docugate init       [--dir <folder>] [--title <text>]
docugate check      [--dir <folder>] [--strict]
docugate openapi    --from <file|url> [--out <file>] 
                    [--include <glob>]... [--exclude <glob>]... 
                    [--redact <name>]... [--check]
docugate tour init  [--max-cost <n>] [--team-id <id>]
docugate tour serve [--port <n>]
docugate tour export <file>
```

**Key Patterns:**
- No external CLI framework
- Manual flag parsing with `VALUE_FLAGS` set to distinguish value flags from booleans
- Supports repeating flags (`--include`, `--exclude`, `--redact`)
- Subcommands via positional args: `command`, `sub`, `sub2`
- Color output helper functions: `red()`, `yellow()`, `green()`, `dim()`
- Uses `spawnSync` to invoke Bob Shell

---

### 4. TOUR FILE FORMAT & PARSING

**Markdown Format** (`src/tour.ts`):

```markdown
---
route: /invoices/:id
title: Invoice
---

## Total
target: [data-tour="invoice-total"]
data: GET /api/invoices/:id → total
code: frontend/src/screens/InvoiceDetail.tsx
source: backend/src/billing.ts
docs: https://example.com/docs

The amount due: computed by totals() in the backend.

## Mark as paid
target: [data-tour="mark-paid"]
data: POST /api/invoices/:id/pay → status
code: frontend/src/screens/InvoiceDetail.tsx

Click to pay.
```

**TypeScript Interfaces** (`src/tour.ts`):

```typescript
export type TourStop = {
  heading: string          // ## heading text
  target: string           // CSS selector, prefer [data-tour="..."]
  data?: string            // "METHOD /path → field" format
  code: string             // Repo-relative file that renders element
  source?: string          // Repo-relative file where value is computed
  docs?: string            // URL to documentation
  prose: string            // Prose explanation
}

export type Tour = {
  route: string            // e.g. /invoices/:id
  title: string            // Screen name
  stops: TourStop[]
  file?: string            // Set by loadTours()
}
```

**Key Functions:**
- `parseTourFile(text: string, file: string): Tour` - Parse markdown to Tour object
- `serializeTourFile(tour: Tour): string` - Serialize Tour back to markdown
- `loadTours(root: string): Tour[]` - Read all .md files from `.docugate/tour/`
- `matchRoute(route: string, pathname: string): boolean` - Match parameterized routes
- `routeToFilename(route: string): string` - Convert `/invoices/:id` → `invoices-id.md`

**Location:** `.docugate/tour/` (directory created during `tour init`)

---

### 5. BOB SHELL INTEGRATION PATTERN

**Tour Init Flow** (`src/tour-init.ts`):

```typescript
export interface TourInitOptions {
  maxCost?: string       // Bobcoin limit (default: '3')
  teamId?: string        // Bob team ID
  runBob?: RunBob        // Dependency injection for testing
}

export type RunBob = (args: string[], cwd: string) => BobRun

interface BobRun {
  status: number | null
  stdout: string
  stderr: string
}

export function tourInit(root: string, options: TourInitOptions = {}): TourInitResult
```

**Setup Steps:**
1. Check Bob Shell installed: `bob --version`
2. Ensure Tour Writer mode and rules in `.bob/custom_modes.yaml` and `.bob/rules-tour-writer/`
3. Create `.docugate/tour/` directory
4. Snapshot existing tour files (SHA256 hash)
5. Run Bob: `bob run --format json --mode tour-writer --max-cost <n> <prompt>`
6. Restore user's modified files if Bob changed them
7. Report setup, added, and restored files

**Error Handling:**
- `BobMissingError` - Bob Shell not installed
- `BobKeyMissingError` - API key required (headless mode)
- Custom mode fallback: If `tour-writer` mode unknown, tries `agent` mode with inline rules

**Mocking in Tests** (`test/tour-init.test.mjs`):

```typescript

  const runBob = (args) => {
    if (args[0] === '--version') return { status: 0, stdout: '1.0.0', stderr: '' }
    // Write files
    return {
      status: 0,
      stdout: JSON.stringify({ 
        status: 'completed', 
        stats: { task_id: 't1', duration_ms: 42000, session_costs: 0.4 },
        last_message: 'done'
      })
    }
  }
  return { calls, runBob }
}
```

**Bob Response Parsing** (`src/tour-init.ts`):

```typescript
interface TourInitResult {
  setup: string[]       // Files created for Tour Writer setup
  added: string[]       // New tour files Bob created
  restored: string[]    // Existing files Bob changed (user versions restored)
  mode: string          // 'tour-writer' or 'agent'
  stats?: {
    durationMs?: number
    cost?: number
    taskId?: string
  }
  lastMessage?: string
}

// Parses last JSON line from Bob's --format json output
function parseBobJson(stdout: string): { stats?, lastMessage? }
```

---

### 6. TYPESCRIPT CONVENTIONS

**`tsconfig.json` Settings:**
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "types": ["node"],
    "rootDir": "src",
    "outDir": "dist",
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "isolatedModules": true
  }
}
```

**Key Conventions:**
- Strict mode enabled
- ES modules with `.js` file extensions in imports: `import { x } from './file.js'`
- Module type: `"module"` in `package.json`
- No default exports; all named exports
- Type definitions in same file as implementation

**Exports Pattern:**
```typescript
// src/init.ts
export type InitResult = { created: string[]; kept: string[]; docsDir: string }
export function init(root: string, opts?: { dir?: string; title?: string }): InitResult { ... }
```

---

### 7. TEST FILE PATTERNS

**Test Framework:** Node's built-in `node:test` module (no external test runner)

export type OpenApiOptions = {
  from: string         // spec file or URL
  output: string       // output file path
  include: string[]
  exclude: string[]
  redact: string[]
}

export type OpenApiResult = {
  spec: Record<string, unknown>
  text: string
  operations: number
  droppedPaths: string[]
  redacted: number
}

export function globToRegExp(glob: string): RegExp
export async function buildOpenApi(root: string, opts: OpenApiOptions): Promise<OpenApiResult>
export async function isCurrent(root: string, output: string, text: string): Promise<boolean>
export function writeOpenApi(root: string, output: string, text: string): void
```

---

## 4. DOCUGATE.JSON SCHEMA & TYPE DEFINITION

**Type**: `src/rules.ts` line 64-77, loaded by `src/config.ts`

```typescript
type DocugateConfig = {
  docsDir?: string              // Docs folder (default: "docs")
  title?: string                // Space title
  sidebar?: string[]            // Order of folders/pages
  api?: {
    generate?: {
      from?: string             // OpenAPI spec URL or file
      output?: string           // Output path (default: "openapi.json")
      include?: string[]        // Path globs to keep
      exclude?: string[]        // Path globs to drop
      redact?: string[]         // Property names to remove
    }
  }
}
```

**Loading**:
- **File location**: `<root>/docugate.json`
- **Parser**: `JSON.parse()` (standard JSON, not YAML)
- **Fallback behavior**: If missing/unreadable, defaults to `{ docsDir: 'docs' }`
- **Validation**: Strict typing at runtime (config.ts lines 46-74)

**How read/written**:
- **Read** (src/config.ts): `readFileSync(path, 'utf8')` → `JSON.parse()`
- **Written** (src/init.ts line 23): `writeFileSync(..., JSON.stringify(config, null, 2) + '\n')`

---

## 5. HOW BOB SHELL IS MOCKED IN TESTS

**File**: `test/tour-init.test.mjs`

### Mock Pattern
```javascript
function fakeBob(root, write, { rejectCustomMode = false } = {}) {
  const calls = []
  const runBob = (args) => {
    // 1. Check --version (pre-flight validation)
    if (args[0] === '--version') return { status: 0, stdout: '1.0.0', stderr: '' }
    
    // 2. Record the call
    calls.push(args)
    
    // 3. Optionally reject custom mode
    const mode = args[args.indexOf('--mode') + 1]
    if (rejectCustomMode && mode !== 'agent') 
      return { status: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `Unknown mode: ${mode}` }
    
    // 4. Simulate Bob writing files
    for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(write)) {
      mkdirSync(join(root, path, '..'), { recursive: true })
      writeFileSync(join(root, path), content)
    }
    
    // 5. Return success JSON
    return ok()  // { status: 0, stdout: JSON.stringify(...) }
  }
  return { calls, runBob }
}
```

### Default Mock Return
```javascript
const ok = (extra = {}) => ({
  status: 0,
  stderr: '',
  stdout: JSON.stringify({
    status: 'completed',
    stats: { task_id: 't1', duration_ms: 42000, session_costs: 0.4 },
    last_message: 'done',
    ...extra
  })
})
```

### Bob Command Args Passed
```javascript
[
  'run',
  '--format', 'json',
  '--workspace', root,
  '--max-cost', '3',
  '--team-id', teamId,          // if provided
  '--mode', 'tour-writer',
  buildPrompt([...before.keys()], false)  // Large prompt string
]
```

### Test Examples
- **Lines 45-66**: Basic setup verification
- **Lines 68-81**: File restoration (user edits preserved)
- **Lines 83-91**: Fallback to agent mode when custom mode rejected
- **Lines 114-120**: Validates Bob check happens before any writes (fail-safe)

---

## 6. TOUR FILE FORMAT & PARSING

**Location**: `.docugate/tour/*.md`

### Format Structure (YAML front matter + stops)
```markdown
---
route: /invoices/:id
title: Invoice
---

## Total
target: [data-tour="invoice-total"]
data: GET /api/invoices/:id → total
code: frontend/src/screens/InvoiceDetail.tsx
source: backend/src/billing.ts
docs: https://example.com/docs

The amount due.

## Mark as paid
target: [data-tour="mark-paid"]
code: frontend/src/screens/InvoiceDetail.tsx

Click to pay.
```

### Parsing Implementation (src/tour.ts lines 36-114)
1. **Front matter** (lines 43-54): Read YAML-like key:value until closing `---`
2. **Stops** (lines 61-111): 
   - Match `## Heading` at start of line
   - Read key:value fields (target, data, code, source, docs)
   - Capture prose (paragraph text after blank line)

### Validation (parsing throws on):
- Missing `route` or `title` in front matter
- Stop missing `target` or `code`

### Round-trip (serializeTourFile, lines 119-142)
- Reconstructs markdown with exact spacing
- Omits optional fields (data, source, docs) when undefined
- Preserves prose exactly as parsed

---

## 7. TYPESCRIPT CONVENTIONS USED

### General
- **strict: true** in tsconfig.json (lines 9)
- **Explicit return types** on all exported functions
- **Type exports** for all public interfaces
- **No default exports** (all named)

### Module System
- **ES modules** ("type": "module" in package.json)
- **File extensions**: Always `.js` in imports (line 3: `'./config.js'`)
- **URL imports**: `import.meta.url` for runtime paths (tour-server.ts line 200)

### Error Handling
- **Custom error classes**: `BobMissingError`, `BobKeyMissingError` (extends Error)
- **Throwing vs. returning**: Errors thrown immediately; non-fatal issues returned in Issue[]
- **No try-catch in most functions**: Errors propagate up

### Data Structures
- **Maps for keyed data**: `Map<string, string[]>` for args
- **Sets for uniqueness**: `Set<string>` for known keys, boolean flags
- **Interfaces for options**: Always `Options` object, never tuple params
- **Union types rare**: Prefer explicit optional properties

### Naming
- **Imperative verbs**: `load`, `parse`, `serialize`, `build`, `start`, `check`
- **Type suffixes**: `*Result`, `*Options`, `*Config`
- **Constants UPPER_CASE**: `TOUR_DIR`, `MODE_SLUG`, `MAX_FILES`

---

## 8. TEST PATTERNS & FIXTURES

### Test Framework
- **Node built-in** (`node:test`, `node:assert/strict`)
- **No external frameworks** (mocha, jest, etc.)
- **Script**: `npm test` runs `npm run build && node --test "test/*.test.mjs"`

### Common Helpers (across test files)
```javascript
// Temp repo creator
function repo(files) {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'docugate-...'))
  for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(files)) {
    mkdirSync(join(dir, path, '..'), { recursive: true })
    writeFileSync(join(dir, path), content)
  }
  return dir
}

// CLI runner
const run = (cwd, ...args) => spawnSync(process.execPath, [CLI, ...args], { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' })
```

### Fixture Structure
```
test/fixtures/
├── tour-parse/
│   ├── simple.md                    # Basic 2-stop tour
│   └── invoice-detail.md            # Full 5-stop tour by Bob
└── tour-check/
    ├── .docugate/tour/*.md          # Valid tours
    ├── backend/                     # Mock backend files
    ├── frontend/                    # Mock frontend files (data-tour attributes)
    └── docs/                        # Docs for check validation
```

### Test Patterns
1. **Isolation**: Each test creates temp dirs, no cleanup needed (tmpdir)
2. **Assertions**: `assert.deepEqual()`, `assert.match()`, `assert.throws()`
3. **Bob mocking**: `fakeBob(root, write)` returns `{ calls, runBob }`
4. **Server testing**: `startServer()` called in tests, closed via `after()` hook

---

## 9. TOUR SERVER HTTP ENDPOINTS

**File**: `src/tour-server.ts`

### Security
- **DNS rebinding protection** (lines 27-50): Host/Origin/Referer must be localhost/127.0.0.1
- **CORS**: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (only for tour data, pill.js)

### Endpoints
```
GET  /tour?path=/invoices/INV-001
     → { route, title, stops }
     → 404 if no matching tour

GET  /events
     → Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream)
     → "connected" immediately, "change" on .docugate/tour/ writes

PUT  /stop
     Body: { route, title?, stop }
     → Upsert tour stop (find by target, update or append)
     → Create/update .docugate/tour/*.md file
     → 200 { ok: true } or 400/500 errors

GET  /pill.js
     → JavaScript from pill/dist/pill.js
     → Served at runtime (location relative to dist/tour-server.js)
```

---

## 10. BUILD & COMPILATION PIPELINE

**Scripts** (package.json):
```bash
npm run build          # tsc -p tsconfig.json && npm run build:pill
npm run build:pill     # tsc -p pill/tsconfig.json && node pill/scripts/bundle.mjs
npm test              # npm run build && node --test "test/*.test.mjs"
```

### Output
- `src/**/*.ts` → `dist/**/*.js` (ES2022, ES modules)
- `pill/src/**/*.ts` → `pill/dist/pill.js` (bundled)

---

## 11. EXACT FILE PATHS SUMMARY

```
src/cli.ts                              (Main CLI entry, 480 LOC)
src/init.ts                             (Repository setup)
src/tour-init.ts                        (Bob integration, 243 LOC)
src/tour.ts                             (Tour parsing/serialization, 198 LOC)
src/tour-server.ts                      (HTTP server, 258 LOC)
src/config.ts                           (docugate.json loading)
src/check.ts                            (Documentation validation)
src/rules.ts                            (Shared rules from app)
src/openapi.ts                          (OpenAPI processing)

test/tour-init.test.mjs                 (Bob mocking patterns)
test/tour.test.mjs                      (Tour parsing tests)
test/tour-server.test.mjs               (Server endpoint tests)
test/cli.test.mjs                       (Integration tests)

test/fixtures/tour-parse/simple.md      (Example: 2-stop tour)
test/fixtures/tour-check/               (Full fixture repo)

package.json                            (ES module, Node 18.17+)
tsconfig.json                           (Strict TS, ES2022)
```

---

## KEY PATTERNS & CONVENTIONS CHECKLIST

✅ **CLI**: Manual parser, Map/Set for args, custom error classes  
✅ **Bob Integration**: Subprocess via `spawnSync()`, file snapshot for protection  
✅ **Config**: Single docugate.json file, JSON (not YAML), optional with safe defaults  
✅ **Tours**: Markdown with YAML front matter, structured parsing, round-trip serialization  
✅ **Tests**: Node built-in, temp dirs, fixtures, fakeBob mocking pattern  
✅ **TypeScript**: Strict mode, explicit types, ES modules, no defaults  
✅ **Error Handling**: Custom error classes, issues array for non-fatal problems  
✅ **Security**: DNS rebinding checks, file path validation
</task_result>

1 | /**
2 |  * How DocuGate reads a repository, restated for the command line.
3 |  *
4 |  * These mirror src/lib/docs.ts and server/github.ts in the DocuGate app. They
5 |  * are copied rather than imported because this package is published on its
6 |  * own; if the app changes how it reads a repository, change them here too, or
7 |  * `docugate check` will pass docs the server then renders differently.
8 |  */
9 | 
10 | /** The server refuses a docs folder with more markdown files than this. */
11 | export const MAX_FILES = 300
12 | 
13 | /** Turn `guides/deploying.md` into `guides/deploying`, and `index.md` into ''. */
14 | export function pathToSlug(path: string): string {
15 |   const withoutExt = path.replace(/\.md$/i, '')
16 |   return withoutExt === 'index' ? '' : withoutExt.replace(/\/index$/i, '')
17 | }
18 | 
19 | /**
20 |  * Resolve a relative markdown link, as authored inside `fromPath`, to the slug
21 |  * DocuGate routes it under. Null for links this does not apply to: external
22 |  * URLs, in-page anchors and anything that is not a markdown file.
23 |  */
24 | export function resolveRelativeLink(href: string, fromPath: string): string | null {
25 |   if (!href || href.startsWith('#')) return null
26 |   if (/^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:/i.test(href) || href.startsWith('//')) return null
27 | 
28 |   const [rawPath] = href.split('#')
29 |   if (!/\.mdx?$/i.test(rawPath)) return null
30 | 
31 |   const dir = fromPath.includes('/') ? fromPath.slice(0, fromPath.lastIndexOf('/')) : ''
32 |   const segments = rawPath.startsWith('/') ? [] : dir.split('/').filter(Boolean)
33 | 
34 |   for (const part of rawPath.split('/')) {
35 |     if (part === '' || part === '.') continue
36 |     if (part === '..') {
37 |       // Climbing above the docs folder leaves it, and DocuGate only serves
38 |       // what is inside it.
39 |       if (!segments.length) return '\0outside'
40 |       segments.pop()
41 |     } else segments.push(part)
42 |   }
43 | 
44 |   return pathToSlug(segments.join('/'))
45 | }
46 | 
47 | /**
48 |  * Where a docs folder has no index.md, its top-level README becomes the
49 |  * landing page — the same file GitHub shows first.
50 |  */
51 | export function landingPath(paths: string[]): string | null {
52 |   const index = paths.find((p) => pathToSlug(p) === '')
53 |   if (index) return index
54 |   return paths.find((p) => !p.includes('/') && /^readme\.md$/i.test(p)) ?? null
55 | }

59 |   const heading = content.match(/^#\s+(.+)$/m)
60 |   return heading ? heading[1].trim() : null

**Setup Steps:**
1. Check Bob Shell installed: `bob --version`
2. Ensure Tour Writer mode and rules in `.bob/custom_modes.yaml` and `.bob/rules-tour-writer/`
3. Create `.docugate/tour/` directory
4. Snapshot existing tour files (SHA256 hash)
5. Run Bob: `bob run --format json --mode tour-writer --max-cost <n> <prompt>`
6. Restore user's modified files if Bob changed them
7. Report setup, added, and restored files

**Error Handling:**
- `BobMissingError` - Bob Shell not installed
- `BobKeyMissingError` - API key required (headless mode)
- Custom mode fallback: If `tour-writer` mode unknown, tries `agent` mode with inline rules

## 5. HOW BOB SHELL IS MOCKED IN TESTS

**File**: `test/tour-init.test.mjs`

### Mock Pattern
```javascript
function fakeBob(root, write, { rejectCustomMode = false } = {}) {
  const calls = []
  const runBob = (args) => {
    // 1. Check --version (pre-flight validation)
    if (args[0] === '--version') return { status: 0, stdout: '1.0.0', stderr: '' }
    
    // 2. Record the call
    calls.push(args)
    
    // 3. Optionally reject custom mode
    const mode = args[args.indexOf('--mode') + 1]
    if (rejectCustomMode && mode !== 'agent') 
      return { status: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `Unknown mode: ${mode}` }
    
    // 4. Simulate Bob writing files
    for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(write)) {
      mkdirSync(join(root, path, '..'), { recursive: true })
      writeFileSync(join(root, path), content)
    }
    
    // 5. Return success JSON
    return ok()  // { status: 0, stdout: JSON.stringify(...) }
  }
  return { calls, runBob }
}
```

## 6. TOUR FILE FORMAT & PARSING

**Location**: `.docugate/tour/*.md`

### Format Structure (YAML front matter + stops)
```markdown
---
route: /invoices/:id
title: Invoice
---

## Total
target: [data-tour="invoice-total"]
data: GET /api/invoices/:id → total
code: frontend/src/screens/InvoiceDetail.tsx

docs: https://example.com/docs

code: frontend/src/screens/InvoiceDetail.tsx

```

### Parsing Implementation (src/tour.ts lines 36-114)
1. **Front matter** (lines 43-54): Read YAML-like key:value until closing `---`
2. **Stops** (lines 61-111): 
   - Match `## Heading` at start of line
   - Read key:value fields (target, data, code, source, docs)
   - Capture prose (paragraph text after blank line)

### Validation (parsing throws on):
- Missing `route` or `title` in front matter
- Stop missing `target` or `code`

### Round-trip (serializeTourFile, lines 119-142)
- Reconstructs markdown with exact spacing
- Omits optional fields (data, source, docs) when undefined
- Preserves prose exactly as parsed

## 7. TYPESCRIPT CONVENTIONS USED

### General
- **strict: true** in tsconfig.json (lines 9)
- **Explicit return types** on all exported functions
- **Type exports** for all public interfaces
- **No default exports** (all named)

### Module System
- **ES modules** ("type": "module" in package.json)
- **File extensions**: Always `.js` in imports (line 3: `'./config.js'`)
- **URL imports**: `import.meta.url` for runtime paths (tour-server.ts line 200)

### Error Handling
- **Custom error classes**: `BobMissingError`, `BobKeyMissingError` (extends Error)
- **Throwing vs. returning**: Errors thrown immediately; non-fatal issues returned in Issue[]
- **No try-catch in most functions**: Errors propagate up

### Data Structures
- **Maps for keyed data**: `Map<string, string[]>` for args
- **Sets for uniqueness**: `Set<string>` for known keys, boolean flags
- **Interfaces for options**: Always `Options` object, never tuple params
- **Union types rare**: Prefer explicit optional properties

### Naming
- **Imperative verbs**: `load`, `parse`, `serialize`, `build`, `start`, `check`
- **Type suffixes**: `*Result`, `*Options`, `*Config`
- **Constants UPPER_CASE**: `TOUR_DIR`, `MODE_SLUG`, `MAX_FILES`

## 9. TOUR SERVER HTTP ENDPOINTS

**File**: `src/tour-server.ts`

### Security
- **DNS rebinding protection** (lines 27-50): Host/Origin/Referer must be localhost/127.0.0.1
- **CORS**: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (only for tour data, pill.js)

### Endpoints
```
GET  /tour?path=/invoices/INV-001
     → { route, title, stops }
     → 404 if no matching tour

GET  /events
     → Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream)
     → "connected" immediately, "change" on .docugate/tour/ writes

PUT  /stop
     Body: { route, title?, stop }
     → Upsert tour stop (find by target, update or append)
     → Create/update .docugate/tour/*.md file
     → 200 { ok: true } or 400/500 errors

GET  /pill.js
     → JavaScript from pill/dist/pill.js
     → Served at runtime (location relative to dist/tour-server.js)
```

177 | function parseBobJson(stdout: string): { stats?: TourInitResult['stats']; lastMessage?: string } {

184 |       const cost = typeof s.session_costs === 'number' ? s.session_costs : s.session_costs?.total

186 |         stats: { durationMs: s.duration_ms, cost: typeof cost === 'number' ? cost : undefined, taskId: s.task_id },

211 |   if (options.teamId) common.push('--team-id', options.teamId)

# docugate init flow — implementation plan

## Overview

Three focused additions to the package:

1. **`src/tour-install.ts`** — a new module that finds the app's HTML/layout entry
   point and injects a dev-only pill loader script, marked with
   `<!-- docugate:pill -->` comment fences so it can be found and removed again.
   Exposed as `docugate tour install [--port n] [--remove]`.

2. **`src/init.ts` (extended)** — the existing `init` function is replaced with a
   richer interactive flow that asks one question at a time, saves `"role"` into
   `docugate.json`, conditionally runs `tourInit` + `tourInstall`, and prints a
   short summary.  The pure library function stays unit-testable; all I/O goes
   through an injectable `IO` interface so tests can drive it without a terminal.

3. **`src/tour-server.ts` (one-liner hint)** — when `docugate tour serve` starts
   and no pill snippet is found, print a one-line hint to run
   `docugate tour install`.

Tests live in `test/tour-install.test.mjs` and `test/init-flow.test.mjs`; they
use the same `repo()` / `fakeBob()` helpers as `test/tour-init.test.mjs`, no
external dependencies, no scratch files left in the repo root.

---

## Sub-task 1 — `src/tour-install.ts` + `docugate tour install`

### Intent
Give developers a single command that adds the DocuGate pill to their app without
touching anything unrelated to the injection point.  The snippet must be
idempotent (running twice is a no-op) and reversible (`--remove` takes it out).

### Expected outcomes
- `src/tour-install.ts` is a standalone TypeScript module exporting `tourInstall`
  and its types/errors.
- `docugate tour install` and `docugate tour install --remove` work end to end.
- `--port` defaults to `4178`; the generated URL is always
  `http://localhost:<port>/pill.js`.
- Running twice leaves the file identical to the first run.
- `--remove` on a file without the snippet is a silent no-op.
- When no HTML/layout is found the function returns `{ target: null }` and the
  CLI prints the one line to paste.

### Todo list

- [ ] Create `src/tour-install.ts` with exported types and `tourInstall` function.
  - Export `TourInstallOptions = { port?: number; remove?: boolean; root?: string }`
  - Export `TourInstallResult = { target: string | null; action: 'inserted' | 'removed' | 'already' | 'none' }`
  - **Pill snippet format** (HTML targets):
    ```
    <!-- docugate:pill -->
    <script>if(location.hostname==='localhost'||location.hostname==='127.0.0.1'){var s=document.createElement('script');s.src='http://localhost:PORT/pill.js';document.head.appendChild(s)}</script>
    <!-- /docugate:pill -->
    ```
    Inserted immediately before `</body>`.
  - **Next.js snippet format** (layout/\_document targets):
    ```tsx
    {/* docugate:pill */}
    {process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' && <script src="http://localhost:PORT/pill.js" />}
    {/* /docugate:pill */}
    ```
    Inserted before the closing `</body>` (or before the last `</html>` tag when
    `</body>` is absent in \_document).
  - **Discovery order** (stop at the first match, skip `node_modules/`, `dist/`,
    `build/`, `.next/`):
    1. `app/layout.tsx`, `app/layout.jsx`
    2. `src/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/layout.jsx`
    3. `pages/_document.tsx`, `pages/_document.jsx`
    4. `index.html` (repo root)
    5. `frontend/index.html`, `client/index.html`, `web/index.html`,
       `app/index.html`, `public/index.html`
  - For discovery: check each candidate path with `existsSync`; return the first
    that exists.
  - For idempotence: search the file content for `<!-- docugate:pill -->` (HTML)
    or `{/* docugate:pill */}` (TSX/JSX).  If found and `remove` is false →
    return `{ action: 'already', target }`.  If found and `remove` is true →
    strip the block and return `{ action: 'removed', target }`.
  - For insert: splice the snippet in before `</body>` (HTML) or before
    `</body>` or `</html>` (TSX/JSX).  If neither tag is found → append to end
    of file (graceful fallback).
  - Never touch any content outside the comment fences.

- [ ] Register `tour install` in `src/cli.ts`:

  - Add `'port'` already in VALUE_FLAGS (already present — no change needed).
  - Handler calls `tourInstall(root, { port, remove })` and prints result.
  - When `target === null` print the pill snippet line to paste.

# docugate init flow — implementation plan

## Overview

Three focused additions to the package:

1. **`src/tour-install.ts`** — a new module that finds the app's HTML/layout entry
   point and injects a dev-only pill loader script, marked with
   `<!-- docugate:pill -->` comment fences so it can be found and removed again.
   Exposed as `docugate tour install [--port n] [--remove]`.

2. **`src/init.ts` (extended)** — the existing `init` function is replaced with a
   richer interactive flow that asks one question at a time, saves `"role"` into
   `docugate.json`, conditionally runs `tourInit` + `tourInstall`, and prints a
   short summary.  The pure library function stays unit-testable; all I/O goes
   through an injectable `IO` interface so tests can drive it without a terminal.

3. **`src/tour-server.ts` (one-liner hint)** — when `docugate tour serve` starts
   and no pill snippet is found, print a one-line hint to run
   `docugate tour install`.

Tests live in `test/tour-install.test.mjs` and `test/init-flow.test.mjs`; they
use the same `repo()` / `fakeBob()` helpers as `test/tour-init.test.mjs`, no
external dependencies, no scratch files left in the repo root.

---

## Sub-task 1 — `src/tour-install.ts` + `docugate tour install`

### Intent
Give developers a single command that adds the DocuGate pill to their app without
touching anything unrelated to the injection point.  The snippet must be
idempotent (running twice is a no-op) and reversible (`--remove` takes it out).

### Expected outcomes
- `src/tour-install.ts` is a standalone TypeScript module exporting `tourInstall`
  and its types/errors.
- `docugate tour install` and `docugate tour install --remove` work end to end.
- `--port` defaults to `4178`; the generated URL is always
  `http://localhost:<port>/pill.js`.
- Running twice leaves the file identical to the first run.
- `--remove` on a file without the snippet is a silent no-op.
- When no HTML/layout is found the function returns `{ target: null }` and the
  CLI prints the one line to paste.

### Todo list

- [ ] Create `src/tour-install.ts` with exported types and `tourInstall` function.
  - Export `TourInstallOptions = { port?: number; remove?: boolean; root?: string }`
  - Export `TourInstallResult = { target: string | null; action: 'inserted' | 'removed' | 'already' | 'none' }`
  - **Pill snippet format** (HTML targets):
    ```
    <!-- docugate:pill -->
    <script>if(location.hostname==='localhost'||location.hostname==='127.0.0.1'){var s=document.createElement('script');s.src='http://localhost:PORT/pill.js';document.head.appendChild(s)}</script>
    <!-- /docugate:pill -->
    ```
    Inserted immediately before `</body>`.
  - **Next.js snippet format** (layout/\_document targets):
    ```tsx
    {/* docugate:pill */}
    {process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' && <script src="http://localhost:PORT/pill.js" />}
    {/* /docugate:pill */}
    ```
    Inserted before the closing `</body>` (or before the last `</html>` tag when
    `</body>` is absent in \_document).
  - **Discovery order** (stop at the first match, skip `node_modules/`, `dist/`,
    `build/`, `.next/`):
    1. `app/layout.tsx`, `app/layout.jsx`
    2. `src/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/layout.jsx`
    3. `pages/_document.tsx`, `pages/_document.jsx`
    4. `index.html` (repo root)
    5. `frontend/index.html`, `client/index.html`, `web/index.html`,
       `app/index.html`, `public/index.html`
  - For discovery: check each candidate path with `existsSync`; return the first
    that exists.
  - For idempotence: search the file content for `<!-- docugate:pill -->` (HTML)
    or `{/* docugate:pill */}` (TSX/JSX).  If found and `remove` is false →
    return `{ action: 'already', target }`.  If found and `remove` is true →
    strip the block and return `{ action: 'removed', target }`.
  - For insert: splice the snippet in before `</body>` (HTML) or before
    `</body>` or `</html>` (TSX/JSX).  If neither tag is found → append to end
    of file (graceful fallback).
  - Never touch any content outside the comment fences.

- [ ] Register `tour install` in `src/cli.ts`:
  - Add `'role'` and `'remove'` to VALUE_FLAGS / bools respectively — actually:
    `role` is a value flag; `remove` and `yes` are booleans.
  - Add `install` as a recognized `sub` for `command === 'tour'`.
  - Add `'port'` already in VALUE_FLAGS (already present — no change needed).
  - Handler calls `tourInstall(root, { port, remove })` and prints result.
  - When `target === null` print the pill snippet line to paste.

## Plan: `docugate init` — unified setup flow

The work is split into **5 sub-tasks**, each independently reviewable:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Sub-task 1\nsrc/tour-install.ts\ndocugate tour install] --> B[Sub-task 2\nsrc/init.ts extended\ndocugate init wizard]
    A --> C[Sub-task 3\ntour serve hint]
    B --> D[Sub-task 4\ntest/tour-install.test.mjs]
    B --> E[Sub-task 5\ntest/init-flow.test.mjs]
    C --> D
```

### Sub-task 1 — `src/tour-install.ts` + `docugate tour install`

New module that discovers the app's HTML / Next.js layout file and injects a dev-only pill loader between `<!-- docugate:pill -->` markers (HTML targets) or `{/* docugate:pill */}` markers (TSX/JSX). Discovery checks these paths in order, skipping `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.next/`:

1. `app/layout.tsx|jsx`, `src/app/layout.tsx|jsx` → Next.js App Router
2. `pages/_document.tsx|jsx` → Next.js Pages Router
3. `index.html` at root → Vite / plain HTML
4. `frontend/`, `client/`, `web/`, `app/`, or `public/` → `index.html`

Inserts before `</body>`; idempotent on the marker strings; `--remove` strips the block; `--port` defaults to `4178`. When nothing is found: returns `{ target: null }` and the CLI prints the one line to paste.

### Sub-task 2 — extend `src/init.ts` + update `docugate init`

Adds `initFlow()` alongside the existing pure `init()` (which stays untouched so `test/cli.test.mjs` keeps passing). The flow:

- **a.** Reads `docugate.json`; if `role` is already saved, skips the question. Otherwise asks `"Is this repository the frontend, the backend, or both?"` (unless `--yes` or no TTY, in which case it defaults to `"both"`).
- **b.** Prints `[coming soon] Sign in to DocuGate and connect this repository.`
- **c.** Frontend / both → offers `tour init` (Bob), then always runs `tour install`. Backend → prints one-liner and skips both.
- **d.** Prints a bullet-list summary + `docugate tour serve` next-step hint.

Injects an `IO` interface (`isTTY`, `ask`, `print`) for testability. Uses `node:readline` — no new dependencies.

Adds `"role"` to `DocugateConfig` in `src/rules.ts` and `KNOWN_KEYS`.

### Sub-task 3 — pill-missing hint in `docugate tour serve`

Adds `hasPillSnippet(root)` to `src/tour-install.ts`. The `case 'serve':` handler in `src/cli.ts` calls it after printing the screen count; if false, prints:
`Hint: run docugate tour install to add the pill to your app automatically.`

### Sub-task 4 — `test/tour-install.test.mjs`

Covers: Vite insert, idempotence, `--remove` (with and without existing snippet), Next.js App Router, Next.js Pages Router, nothing-found, and `hasPillSnippet`.

### Sub-task 5 — `test/init-flow.test.mjs`

Covers: frontend / backend / both roles, second-run skips question, `--yes`, CI (no TTY), Vite + Next app router + pages router fixtures, backend skip message. Uses injected `IO` and `fakeBob` mocks.

---

The plan file is at [`docugate-init-flow-plan.md`](docugate-init-flow-plan.md).

**Questions before approving:**

1. The plan uses **`"both"` as the CI/`--yes` default role** (since the project could be either). Should the default be something different, e.g. `"frontend"`?
2. When `--yes` is passed and the role is `frontend`/`both`, the plan **always runs tour install without asking** — is that the right behaviour, or should `--yes` skip only the role question and still prompt for the tour steps?
3. For the Next.js snippet, the plan inserts a self-closing `<script src="…" />`. Should it use `<Script>` (Next.js `next/script`) instead, or stay as a plain `<script>` JSX element to avoid an import addition?

Plan approved, with these answers and two changes:

1. Default role: with --yes and no --role, use "both". With no terminal (CI) and no --role, don't guess: write docugate.json without a role and print that --role sets it.
2. --yes runs every step, including the Bob tour and tour install. That is the point of one command. Without --yes, ask before the Bob tour (it costs Bobcoins) and before editing the app's file.
3. Next.js: keep a plain <script src="http://localhost:<port>/pill.js" async /> inside the development check. No next/script import, so nothing else in the file changes.
Change 1: when tour init finds screens but Bob Shell is missing or fails, don't stop the whole setup. Say what went wrong and how to retry (docugate tour init), then still run tour install and finish with the summary.
Change 2: save the plan as bob_sessions/docugate_task05_one_command_plan.md, not in the repo root.

+import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
+import { join } from 'node:path'
+
+// `docugate tour install` inserts a development-only pill loader into the
+// app's HTML or Next.js layout entry point. The snippet is wrapped in comment
+// markers so it can be found and removed again without touching anything else.
+
+export const DEFAULT_PORT = 4178
+
+// Comment markers used as anchors — one pair for HTML files, one for TSX/JSX.
+const HTML_OPEN = '<!-- docugate:pill -->'
+const HTML_CLOSE = '<!-- /docugate:pill -->'
+const JSX_OPEN = '{/* docugate:pill */}'
+const JSX_CLOSE = '{/* /docugate:pill */}'
+
+/** Candidate paths checked in order. The first one that exists wins. */
+export const CANDIDATES = [
+  'app/layout.tsx',
+  'app/layout.jsx',
+  'src/app/layout.tsx',
+  'src/app/layout.jsx',
+  'pages/_document.tsx',
+  'pages/_document.jsx',
+  'index.html',
+  'frontend/index.html',
+  'client/index.html',
+  'web/index.html',
+  'app/index.html',
+  'public/index.html',
+] as const
+
+export type TourInstallOptions = {
+  port?: number
+  remove?: boolean
+}
+
+export type TourInstallResult = {
+  /** The file that was (or would be) modified; null when nothing was found. */
+  target: string | null
+  action: 'inserted' | 'removed' | 'already' | 'none'
+}
+
+/** Returns true if any candidate file already contains the pill snippet. */
+export function hasPillSnippet(root: string): boolean {
+  for (const rel of CANDIDATES) {
+    const abs = join(root, rel)
+    if (!existsSync(abs)) continue
+    const text = readFileSync(abs, 'utf8')
+    if (text.includes(HTML_OPEN) || text.includes(JSX_OPEN)) return true
+  }
+  return false
+}
+
+function isJsx(rel: string): boolean {
+  return rel.endsWith('.tsx') || rel.endsWith('.jsx')
+}
+
+function makeSnippet(port: number, jsx: boolean): string {
+  if (jsx) {
+    const url = `http://localhost:${port}/pill.js`
+    return (
+      `\n      ${JSX_OPEN}\n` +
+      `      {process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' && <script src="${url}" async />}\n` +
+      `      ${JSX_CLOSE}`
+    )
+  }
+  const url = `http://localhost:${port}/pill.js`
+  return (
+    `\n  ${HTML_OPEN}\n` +
+    `  <script>if(location.hostname==='localhost'||location.hostname==='127.0.0.1'){` +
+    `var s=document.createElement('script');s.src='${url}';document.head.appendChild(s)}</script>\n` +
+    `  ${HTML_CLOSE}`
+  )
+}
+
+function insertSnippet(text: string, snippet: string, jsx: boolean): string {
+  // Find the last </body> tag and insert immediately before it.
+  const tag = '</body>'
+  const idx = text.lastIndexOf(tag)
+  if (idx !== -1) {
+    return text.slice(0, idx) + snippet + '\n' + text.slice(idx)
+  }
+  if (jsx) {
+    // _document.tsx may close with </html> instead of </body>
+    const htmlIdx = text.lastIndexOf('</html>')
+    if (htmlIdx !== -1) {
+      return text.slice(0, htmlIdx) + snippet + '\n' + text.slice(htmlIdx)
+    }
+  }
+  // Graceful fallback: append to end of file.
+  return text + snippet + '\n'
+}
+
+function removeSnippet(text: string, open: string, close: string): string {
+  const start = text.indexOf(open)
+  if (start === -1) return text
+  const end = text.indexOf(close, start)
+  if (end === -1) return text
+  // Also eat the leading newline before the open marker if present.
+  const before = start > 0 && text[start - 1] === '\n' ? start - 1 : start
+  return text.slice(0, before) + text.slice(end + close.length)
+}
+
+/**
+ * Installs (or removes) the dev-only pill loader snippet in the app's entry
+ * point. Safe to run multiple times — running it again when the snippet is
+ * already present is a no-op.
+ */
+export function tourInstall(root: string, options: TourInstallOptions = {}): TourInstallResult {
+  const port = options.port ?? DEFAULT_PORT
+  const remove = options.remove ?? false
+
+  for (const rel of CANDIDATES) {
+    const abs = join(root, rel)
+    if (!existsSync(abs)) continue
+
+    const jsx = isJsx(rel)
+    const open = jsx ? JSX_OPEN : HTML_OPEN
+    const close = jsx ? JSX_CLOSE : HTML_CLOSE
+
+    const original = readFileSync(abs, 'utf8')
+    const hasMarker = original.includes(open)
+
+    if (remove) {
+      if (!hasMarker) return { target: rel, action: 'already' }
+      const updated = removeSnippet(original, open, close)
+      writeFileSync(abs, updated)
+      return { target: rel, action: 'removed' }
+    }
+
+    if (hasMarker) return { target: rel, action: 'already' }
+
+    const snippet = makeSnippet(port, jsx)
+    const updated = insertSnippet(original, snippet, jsx)
+    writeFileSync(abs, updated)
+    return { target: rel, action: 'inserted' }
+  }
+
+  return { target: null, action: 'none' }
+}
+
+/** The one-line snippet to paste manually when no entry point was found. */
+export function pillSnippetLine(port: number): string {
+  return `<script>if(location.hostname==='localhost'||location.hostname==='127.0.0.1'){var s=document.createElement('script');s.src='http://localhost:${port}/pill.js';document.head.appendChild(s)}</script>`
+}

+import { createInterface } from 'node:readline'
+import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
+import { basename, join } from 'node:path'
+import { CONFIG_FILE, loadConfig } from './config.js'
+import type { RunBob } from './tour-init.js'
+import { tourInit, BobMissingError, BobKeyMissingError } from './tour-init.js'
+import { tourInstall, pillSnippetLine, DEFAULT_PORT } from './tour-install.js'
+import type { TourInitResult } from './tour-init.js'
+import type { TourInstallResult } from './tour-install.js'
+
+export type InitResult = { created: string[]; kept: string[]; docsDir: string }
+
+/**
+ * Sets a repository up for DocuGate: a docugate.json, and a first page if the
+ * docs folder has none. Never overwrites — running it twice is harmless, and
+ * running it in a repository that already has docs only adds what is missing.
+ */
+export function init(root: string, opts: { dir?: string; title?: string } = {}): InitResult {
+  const created: string[] = []
+  const kept: string[] = []
+  const existing = loadConfig(root)
+  const docsDir = (opts.dir ?? existing.docsDir).replace(/^\/|\/$/g, '') || 'docs'
+  const title = opts.title ?? basename(root)
+
+  if (existing.found) {
+    kept.push(CONFIG_FILE)
+  } else {
+    const config = { docsDir, title }
+    writeFileSync(join(root, CONFIG_FILE), JSON.stringify(config, null, 2) + '\n')
+    created.push(CONFIG_FILE)
+  }
+
+  const base = join(root, docsDir)
+  const hasMarkdown =
+    existsSync(base) && readdirSync(base, { recursive: true }).some((f) => /\.md$/i.test(String(f)))
+
+  if (hasMarkdown) {
+    kept.push(`${docsDir}/`)
+  } else {
+    mkdirSync(base, { recursive: true })
+    writeFileSync(
+      join(base, 'index.md'),
+      `# ${title}\n\nWelcome. This page is the landing page of your DocuGate space.\n\n` +
+        `Every \`.md\` file in \`${docsDir}/\` becomes a page, and every folder becomes a\n` +
+        `section in the sidebar. The first \`# heading\` in a file is its title.\n`,
+    )
+    created.push(`${docsDir}/index.md`)
+  }
+
+  return { created, kept, docsDir }
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Interactive setup flow
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+export type Role = 'frontend' | 'backend' | 'both'
+
+/** Minimal I/O surface so the flow can be driven by tests without a terminal. */
+export interface IO {
+  isTTY: boolean
+  ask(question: string, defaultAnswer: string): Promise<string>
+  print(line: string): void
+}
+
+export interface InitFlowOptions {
+  dir?: string
+  title?: string
+  role?: Role
+  yes?: boolean
+  port?: number

+  runBob?: RunBob

+export interface InitFlowResult {

+  kept: string[]
+  docsDir: string
+  role: Role | undefined
+  tourResult?: TourInitResult
+  tourError?: string
+  installResult?: TourInstallResult

+
+function makeDefaultIO(): IO {
+  const isTTY = Boolean(process.stdin.isTTY)
+  return {
+    isTTY,
+    ask(question, defaultAnswer) {
+      return new Promise((resolve) => {
+        const rl = createInterface({ input: process.stdin, output: process.stdout })
+        rl.question(`${question} `, (answer) => {
+          rl.close()
+          resolve(answer.trim() || defaultAnswer)
+        })
+      })
+    },
+    print(line) {
+      console.log(line)
+    },
+  }
+}
+
+function saveRole(root: string, role: Role): void {
+  const path = join(root, CONFIG_FILE)
+  let existing: Record<string, unknown> = {}
+  if (existsSync(path)) {
+    try {
+      existing = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')) as Record<string, unknown>
+    } catch {
+      // leave as empty object; will be overwritten with role added
+    }
+  }
+  existing.role = role
+  writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(existing, null, 2) + '\n')

+const VALID_ROLES = new Set<string>(['frontend', 'backend', 'both'])
+
+/**
+ * Runs the full interactive DocuGate setup wizard. Asks one short question,
+ * saves the result in docugate.json, conditionally runs tour init and tour
+ * install, and prints a summary.
+ */
+export async function initFlow(root: string, options: InitFlowOptions = {}): Promise<InitFlowResult> {
+  const io = options.io ?? makeDefaultIO()
+  const yes = options.yes ?? false
+  const port = options.port ?? DEFAULT_PORT
+
+  // ── Step 1: base repo setup (docugate.json + docs/) ──────────────────────
+  const base = init(root, { dir: options.dir, title: options.title })
+

+  const loaded = loadConfig(root)
+  const savedRole = loaded.config.role
+
+  let role: Role | undefined = savedRole ?? options.role
+
+  if (!role) {

+      io.print(`  docugate.json written. Set the repository role with --role frontend|backend|both.`)

+      return { ...base, role: undefined }

+export function init(root: string, opts: { dir?: string; title?: string } = {}): InitResult {
+  const created: string[] = []
+  const kept: string[] = []
+  const existing = loadConfig(root)

+  const title = opts.title ?? basename(root)

+    kept.push(CONFIG_FILE)
+  } else {

+        `section in the sidebar. The first \`# heading\` in a file is its title.\n`,

data.content:
All 117 tests pass. Here's what was built:

---

## What changed

### New files
- **[`src/tour-install.ts`](src/tour-install.ts)** — `tourInstall()`, `hasPillSnippet()`, `pillSnippetLine()`. Discovers app entry points in a fixed candidate order, inserts/removes the dev-only pill snippet between comment markers, fully idempotent.
- **[`test/tour-install.test.mjs`](test/tour-install.test.mjs)** — 14 tests: Vite insert, idempotence, `--remove` with/without snippet, `public/index.html`, Next.js app router, Next.js pages router, nothing-found, `hasPillSnippet`, custom port.
- **[`test/init-flow.test.mjs`](test/init-flow.test.mjs)** — 15 tests: all 5 scenarios from the plan plus edge cases; Bob and IO are fully injected — no real terminal or real Bob Shell touched.

### Modified files
- **[`src/rules.ts`](src/rules.ts)** — added `role?: 'frontend' | 'backend' | 'both'` to `DocugateConfig` and `'role'` to `KNOWN_KEYS`.
- **[`src/init.ts`](src/init.ts)** — `init()` unchanged; added `IO` interface, `InitFlowOptions`, `InitFlowResult`, and `initFlow()` which drives the wizard with injectable I/O and Bob.
- **[`src/cli.ts`](src/cli.ts)** — wired `tour install`, updated `case 'init':` to call `initFlow`, added `--role`/`--yes` to the parser and help, added pill-missing hint to `tour serve`, and updated the unknown-subcommand error.

### Key behaviours per the approved spec
| Scenario | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `--yes`, no `--role` | role = `"both"`, runs Bob + install without prompting |
| `--yes`, with `--role` | uses that role |
| CI (no TTY), no `--role` | writes `docugate.json` without role, prints `--role` guidance, exits |
| Bob missing / fails | prints warning + retry hint (`docugate tour init`), continues to install + summary |
| `tour serve`, no pill | prints hint `run docugate tour install` |
| Second `docugate init` | role already in config → skips question entirely |
